the role of rheumatoid arthritis immune complexes in the stimulation of IgM production and IgM rheumatofactor (RF) production by B lymphocytes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RA IC stimulate the production of both IgM and IgRF from normal B lymphocytes.
RA IC can induce IgM and IgG RF production by human B lymphocytes.
RA IC are able to stimulate the production from normal B lymphocytes of both IgM and IgG RF and to inhibit B cell proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rheumatoid arthritis sera contain immune complexes which stimulate the production of rheumatoid factor and inhibit the proliferation of B lymphocytes.

rheumatoid arthritis IC stimulate the production of rheumatoid factor by B cells and that this stimulation requires de novo protein synthesis and that the stimulation of IgM production is associated with inhibition of B cell proliferation.
the stimulation of IgM production by rheumatoid factor (RF) is mediated through a complement-activating mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rheumatoid arthritis is an immune disease that is driven by the immune complexes that are formed in the body.
the immune system is not a simple on/off switch.
rheumatoid factor can be produced from B lymphocytes in response to immune complexes.
